speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the Ministry can require career coaches to handhold jobseekers, especially our low-wage workers, till they find jobs as it is reassuring to jobseekers knowing that there are employment professionals they can turn to who can provide guidance and support to them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government is providing substantial employment support to help Singaporeans stay in work, such as through the Jobs Support Scheme and programmes to help them be re-skilled and redeployed to new roles.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Around 33,100 jobseekers have been placed thus far and the efforts are continuing.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In this period of weakness in the job market, these efforts have been a very useful supplement to the normal recruitment activities that take place on their own.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked whether more personalised support can be given to jobseekers, especially low-wage workers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We appreciate this is not an easy time for jobseekers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To help them in their search, we have very quickly expanded the touchpoints to be readily accessible in every HDB town.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When they first visit our touchpoints, jobseekers are provided with basic career advisory and job search assistance, and are also invited to take an assessment on their career readiness.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Jobseekers may be assessed to require more intensive support before they are ready to start the job search, or may request for more support even if they are assessed to be ready.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Such jobseekers are provided with one-to-one career coaching.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our career coaches provide tailored support to these jobseekers, which may include referring them to supplementary programmes, such as motivational or interview training workshops.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At an appropriate time, career coaches will help them be matched to suitable opportunities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This process takes longer for some jobseekers than others.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our career coaches will hand-hold the jobseekers while helping them find their footing and gain independence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Post-placement, our career coaches conduct check-ins to ensure that they are settling well into their new workplaces.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: WSG has also been proactively reaching out to all applicants for the COVID-19 Support Grant or CSG and, together with the MSF and the People's Association, to families living in rental housing.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Households that need employment assistance are referred to WSG.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Through these targeted outreach efforts, about 6,000 individuals have taken up our career matching services, which may include one-to-one coaching for those less job-ready.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked how many senior workers have benefited from the WorkPro Job Redesign Grant or JRG.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With employers today having a better appreciation of job redesign to create more inclusive workplaces, we have discontinued WorkPro JRG.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This does not mean there is no longer a need for job re-design, but it can be equally well-supported through the Enterprise Development Grant and Productivity Solutions Grant or PSG.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, the PSG will be further expanded later this year to support job redesign consultancy services, on top of companies' own job redesign efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Whether through the JRG or other programmes, the Government will provide a higher level of support to employers of seniors to help such workers stay in work.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, the recently announced Jobs Growth Incentive provides employers of new hires aged 40 and above double the wage support for other new local hires.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This comes on top of the Special Employment Credit for workers aged 55 and above.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Where seniors need skills top-ups to be recruited or retraining to support business transformation, the level of funding is generally higher.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Employers that formalise a higher retirement age or part-time re-employment in their HR policies can also enjoy grant support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These initiatives together help to address employers' concerns about the cost of seniors in their workforce and the practical adjustments they must make to have age-friendly workplaces.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In every way possible, we will try to enhance the attractiveness of seniors so they can keep working if they wish.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo is looking ahead to next year.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He asks what is being done to prepare students majoring in aerospace-, aviation- and hospitality-related disciplines who are graduating in 2021.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Like Mr Choo, we are closely monitoring the employment outcomes of graduating students.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MOE's Graduate Employment Survey for graduates in 2020 will be published in the first quarter of 2021.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will give some indication as to the prospects for the cohort graduating in 2021.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the meantime, the Institutes of Higher Learning or IHLs have started comprehensive career guidance and assistance programmes to prepare students who are graduating next year.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In particular, they will get help to navigate adjacent career opportunities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Meaning, those that are not specifically targeted at their disciplines but adjacent to it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are organising career fairs that feature job openings in adjacent sectors which will make good use of the graduates' education and skills.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The IHLs are also introducing new electives for students to equip them with emerging cross-sector skills such as data analytics and visualisation, programming as well as digital marketing – skills which are sought after generally.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As a pre-emptive move to supplement job availability, the Government introduced the SGUnited Traineeships Programme which has curated more than 21,000 traineeship places from about 3,300 host organisations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Candidates will also have better opportunities if they are open to trying out positions outside of the disciplines they are trained in, or look beyond positions that many applicants have focused on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to watch the situation closely and adjust the programme accordingly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Although there may still be retrenchments and job losses, it is not all gloom and doom.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is what they usually want and central to how we sustain support for Singaporeans on an on-going basis.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, could MOM supplement the SGUnited jobs initiative with more manned hotlines, where jobseekers can dial in for career advice and job-matching?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This would be very helpful for our workers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second, again to help our older low-income workers, it would be helpful if the Ministry makes provision for career coaches to be conversant in the mother tongue languages and even dialects, if this is not already done.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The second one, our career coaches are already equipped with a number of languages.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, if they come across a client whom they have difficulty conversing with because of the language barrier, they will certainly refer the client to another colleague, in order to be able to provide the requisite assistance to the jobseeker.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To the question of hotlines, WSG has manned phone lines for jobseekers who would like to dial in for more information or who wish to seek further assistance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These are available from Mondays to Fridays between 8.30 am and 5.30 pm, as well as on Saturdays from 8.30 am to 1 pm.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Jobseekers may also submit their enquiries via WSG's feedback portal.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But I would like to thank Ms Pereira for her suggestion and that is to make this line more readily known so that jobseekers know that this is an avenue that they can also look for.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I thank her for the suggestions and I will work with WSG to see how best to do so.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I appreciate the efforts of the Government in supporting re-employment and in redesigning jobs.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While we have been encouraging companies to redesign job for seniors through various grants and schemes throughout the years, the pace at which companies are proactively redesigning jobs, I think that can be improved.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: So, jobs for seniors become actively designed for the transforming industries.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They have been very much a focus of my Ministry's work.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The hon Member mentioned that in the Industry Transformation Maps or ITMs, can we make special emphasis and give special consideration to this group of workers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, the ITM has a very deliberate track called the jobs and skills track that looks at different segments of our workforce, whether they are the low-wage workers or seniors or PMEs or women.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Actually, there are specific work programmes that are targeted at enabling each of these segments to stay productive at work and also to upskill them so that, if they so wish, they can remain in the workforce.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are specific work streams to address each of these workforce segments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To his question about whether we can get the employers to step up their redesign efforts, it is very much aligned with the Government's thinking.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our experience is that for the companies that already have a very large segment of their workforce that are in their 40s, 50s and perhaps even older, these companies do recognise the need for them to step up in terms of redesigning the work.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They know very well that when their seniors retire and if the seniors retire because not enough effort has been put into redesigning the workplace, then they stand to lose a very valuable part of the workforce.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I have actually visited a lot of companies that are quite deliberate in how they go about doing so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Meaning that the companies need not only depend on their own understanding of how to do job redesign.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are actually prepared to fund a consultant coming on board to help them think through the job redesign process.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we will continue to look for opportunities to strengthen our companies' abilities to conduct job redesign because, if you look at our senior employment rate, it has actually improved over the decades.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We want to make sure that we build on these gains.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Seniors also tell us that they wish to continue working and job redesign is one part of it; skills enhancement is another part of it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And another very practical thing that seniors also tell us is that whilst they want to continue working, it may not be to the same intensity as before.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, in addition to job redesign, we have also invested in efforts to ask companies to see how those jobs can be designed in such a way that even on a part-time basis the seniors can continue.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we will continue to look out for more opportunities to enhance senior employment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It has tended to be more of that sort of nature of difficulties.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are, of course, also certain reasons why some seniors may not be able to move on to jobs that pay higher.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That could be a question of their skills deficits.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And one of the things that we have noticed, for example, is that when we were carrying out the work for the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers, more so than other segments of the workforce, seniors are very dependent on what their employers indicate to them are training needs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And apart from what the employers indicate as training needs, seniors are less likely to initiate training on their own.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That may be one reason why it has been harder for them to access a wider range of jobs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But for the same work, actually, the bigger risk has been that the seniors, not necessarily having a lot more skills and competencies, earn more.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we have, over the years, worked very hard to try and encourage companies to move towards a competency-based wage structure rather than a seniority-based wage structure.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A seniority-based wage structure certainly gives an individual the sense of comfort that, as he advances with the company, he is being recognised.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This way, it allows for the employer and the senior workers to reset the terms upon which they can continue this employment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If I may riff off the Member Mr Sharael Taha's question.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am wondering what the Ministry in particular has done to support older jobseekers who have lost their jobs at an age relatively close to retirement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, perhaps something like in 61 or 62 but who still wish to continue working not so much in a different job which requires redesign but actually within the same job and they may be facing certain kinds of discriminatory practices because they are close to the retirement age.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: By and large, if you look at how we help jobseekers, whether they are younger or not so young, if they want to get back into the same job role or same sector which has already seen quite a lot of displacements, then the barriers will be quite high because the fact that they were displaced does suggest that, in that particular sector, it is already not doing so well.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is not targeted specifically only at more senior jobseekers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: All jobseekers will benefit from keeping an open mind and being willing to consider transiting into other sectors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One thing that we have found to be quite encouraging is that where the senior workers are willing just like any other jobseeker or jobseekers of any other age and the employees can see the enthusiasm and the willingness to learn, actually, quite a large number of them have been able to take part in our conversion programmes and to enter new job roles or new sectors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I have very often encountered participants in our Professional Conversion Programmes or our Place-and-Train programme who are in their late 50s and even in their early 60s.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And whenever there are cases where they felt that they were not fairly considered, we would encourage them to approach MOM and we will reach out to the employer to understand how to support them better so that all jobseekers know that they are being considered fairly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For the students who are still studying, naturally, I think they are quite worried about the employment situation when they come out.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: One, for those who are still studying, they have reflected that there is a lack of internship and attachment opportunities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: So, that might affect their employability when you come out.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: They are naturally worried that when they come out, would they still be able to have as good a set of skills in the marketplace and will going to adjacent sectors erode their competencies over time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The second point is that they will come out in 2021, competing with existing workers with experience and they do not have those.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I wonder if the Ministry can come up with programmes that will allow them to not only just maintain their current competency but also to catch up with their assisting peers in the industry so that we do lose our aviation, aerospace and hospitality competency over time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I was in MOT when we encouraged many Singaporean youths to take up opportunities in this sector because we considered the growth prospects to be very promising.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Singapore is booming as an air hub and we are working very hard to allow our air hub to recover and I certainly hope that the situation stabilises to the point where there is better clarity to all the young people who have taken on opportunities in these sectors for training.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Since Mr Choo asked, I had also enquired what about internships right now as they give a useful indication as to the adaptation that we can make.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Of course, it would be better if all of them were to be able to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But, given the circumstances where the companies' activities have gone down a lot, that would not be realistic.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But half of them still being able to get such an internship is not bad.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have not given up on helping them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Their skills in engineering are actually very widely usable in other sectors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: About 60% have got useful skills that allow them to intern in roles that tap on their understanding of business management, for example.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, they have been able to get meaningful internship opportunities even if it is not directly involved in Aviation Management.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is in relation to how these students can be taken care of.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo had a second part of his question and, that is, subsequent to these opportunities, supposing these students would like to return to their areas of study or return to an area of work that is more related to their discipline, will there be opportunities to do so?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think our record has been that whenever the industry has a need and there are people who would like to join the industry, then we will make available career conversion programmes and, if there is a demand for such students to return to the sector and some top-up is required, then I would like to assure Mr Choo that every effort will be made to avail such programmes to them.
